content:
Sarah K: Hey team, GroceryCorp just opened a high-priority ticket — their embeddings calls have been failing intermittently for the past 3 hours. Error from their client: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768". They say this started after they switched regions to eu-west-1.

Ellie (CS): I have the customer repro. They call our embeddings endpoint with model=redwood-embed-1, region=eu-west-1, batch_size=64. It started failing when they scaled up to batch_size 64.

Diego (SRE): dimension mismatch + region change + batching = smells like a routing or model-variant mismatch. Could be that eu-west pool is serving a quantized/legacy variant with 768 dims while our API accepts 1536 for the main variant.

Matt I (Infra): Quick check — deploy bot shows eu-west-1 has a smaller model variant rolled out last night (canary). deploy-bot: rolled redwood-embed-1-small -> eu-west-1 @ 02:14 UTC (canary 20%).

Sarah K: @Matt I any chance the router is returning that canary variant for production customers? GroceryCorp is on standard hosted plan.

Matt I (Infra): Possibly. Our smart routing policy picks variants by capacity and latency. If eu-west capacity is low, requests may spill to the small variant. That variant has 768 dims.

Diego (SRE): Confirming with logs. From ingress traces:
```
2026-03-14T10:22:03Z INFO route selected: eu-west-1-pool-A -> variant=redwood-embed-1-small
2026-03-14T10:22:03Z ERROR model::infer: incompatible-output-dimensions requested=1536 got=768
```

Ellie (CS): Customer client stack shows the SDK validates vector size after the call, which is why they see dimension errors. But the model produced smaller vectors when routed to small variant.

Sarah K: They also complain about latency spikes and some 5xxs around same time. Could be cold starts causing spillover?

Diego (SRE): Yes — eu-west capacity was at 92% around the incident window per metrics. Cold starts for the full model are higher memory so we route to small to avoid queuing. That causes dimension mismatch. Bad combination.

Matt I (Infra): Immediate mitigations: 1) pin GroceryCorp to the main variant in eu-west (force model=redwood-embed-1:full) 2) adjust routing policy to avoid variant with different output dims for same model name 3) bump dedicated capacity for eu-west or enable burst.

Sarah K: Which one can we do right now for the customer? They want a hotfix fast.

Diego (SRE): I can add a temporary route override for their API key to prefer the full variant. Will do a safe routing ACL.

Matt I (Infra): I'll rollback the canary in eu-west to 0% until we have a dimensional compatibility check in the rollout pipeline.

Ellie (CS): I'll tell the customer to set a short-term workaround: set batch_size <= 16 and pin model explicitly (python snippet):
```python
client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-1:full", inputs=batch, region="eu-west-1")
```
This reduces exposure to the small variant and avoids large batches that expose routing differences.

Sarah K: Can someone reproduce locally? Customer provided curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-groc-XXXX' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["a","b"],"batch_size":64, "region":"eu-west-1"}'
```
When routed to small variant it returns 768-length vectors.

Diego (SRE): Repro confirmed in staging by routing with the canary. Created a short postmortem note and added traces.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued for eu-west-1 canary -> user Matt I approved.

Matt I (Infra): Rollback initiated. Also opened infra ticket INF-444 to make variant-output-dimension part of deployment gating.

Diego (SRE): Root cause summary: our routing policy allowed serving a differently-parameterized variant under the same model name during capacity pressure. That variant emits embeddings of different dimensionality, causing client-side validation failures. Cold starts increased spillover to small variant.

Ellie (CS): Customer is worried about billing — they retried and consumed extra tokens/embeddings. Any guidance?

Sarah K: We'll credit their overage for the retry window. I'll open billing ticket and flag for review.

Matt I (Infra): Action items:
- (Infra) INF-444: add dimension compatibility check to rollout pipeline and fail canary if mismatch.
- (SRE) SRE-789: add routing rule to disallow serving variant with different output dims under same model name.
- (Support) SUP-210: credit customer retries and confirm workaround applied.

Diego (SRE): Longer term: we should include a lightweight model metadata handshake in the routing path — return output_dim in negotiate response so clients can detect mismatch earlier and fall back.

Sarah K: Ellie, confirm with GroceryCorp when rollback + pinning done and ask them to re-run their heavy job. I'll keep them posted.

Ellie (CS): Done — told them to wait ~5m after rollback. They hit success after that and confirmed vectors are 1536 length. They also saw latency normalize.

Sarah K: Thanks team. I'll mark the ticket resolved after billing credit. Closing notes to add to knowledge base: include region routing checks in support runbook and example repro curl.

Diego (SRE): Adding monitoring alert: alert when model name served across variants with differing output dims.

Matt I (Infra): And I'll change canary rollout notes — explicitly call out output-dimension compatibility.

Sarah K: Great. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:

embeddings-bot: Incident closed (reference INF-444, SRE-789, SUP-210).
